A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–Q. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original bias measurements for four MLMs, retraining experiments, and comparisons with human annotations, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including pretrained and retrained MLM bias scores, ROC curves, and statistical comparisons.

M1.justification: The iterative masking procedure, log-probability difference, attention-weighted measures, BSPT, and BSRT are unchanged. The modified ∆P highlighted in v3 already appears in v2 Equation 3.

E1.justification: Both retain the nine CPS categories, four StereoSet intrasentence categories, and CPS retraining scenarios. However, v2 Table 17 contains an undefined 'AA' row that disappears from v3 Table 18. Its unspecified population prevents determining whether its removal changes coverage or only removes an extraneous result.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain CSPS, SSS, AUL, AULA, CRR, CRRA, ∆P, and ∆PA where applicable. Repositioning CRR as a comparator does not change its existing participation in the experiments.

E3.justification: The four models, preprocessing, 80/20 retraining split, 0.15 masking probability, 30 epochs, and classification procedures remain unchanged. Appendix P.1 repeats settings previously reported in v2’s Section 3.5 footnote.

E4.justification: The ECDF comparisons, race-bias analysis, human-annotation ROC analysis, and worked examples are retained. New Table 3 summarizes existing retraining sensitivity results; the detailed discussion largely moves to Appendix P.2.

E5.justification: Both use the same Shapiro–Wilk, McNemar, and Welch tests and significance thresholds. Retained result rows have identical significance markers. Additional summaries and highlighting introduce no new statistical procedure, repeated-run information, or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results and all five figures match, but v3 removes the seven 'AA' scores from v2 Table 17 and adds aggregate findings. New Section 4.5 incorrectly assigns Sadv nonsignificance counts of 1/12/13 to AUL/AULA/CSPS; Tables 15–18 give 12/13/1. It also reports four AUL scores strictly above 50, although the tables contain three and one equal to 50.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and bounds are retained. Sentence indexing changes from subscripts to parentheses are equivalent notation. Added explanations of logarithms and attention provide motivation without new formal results or derivations.

C1.justification: v3’s introduction and conclusion explicitly claim that ∆PA, CRRA, and modified ∆P are more sensitive than CRR, while retaining CRR in the accurate retraining-bias measurement group. The introduction also suggests applicability after fine-tuning on other objectives. The central scoring contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking logarithms to sensitivity to low-probability tokens and attention-head averaging to reduced individual-head noise. It suggests use after other fine-tuning objectives and explicitly restricts the religious-bias interpretation involving AUL/AULA to BERTunc. The limitations section is substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, software, model identifiers, preprocessing, training details, and package-release information remain unchanged. Appendix P.1 relocates existing settings, and the PDFs contain the same external hyperlink targets.

R1.justification: The cited works are unchanged. v3 more consistently distinguishes Salutari et al.’s CRR from the proposed attention-weighted measures and positions the latter as more sensitive than CRR, refining the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative by separating Methodology from Experiments and Findings, consolidating related work, rewriting the abstract and retraining-results discussion, and moving detailed discussion and settings into Appendix P.

P2.justification: v3 adds summary Table 3, reverses Table 2’s shading and corrects its 'D-' definition to 'distilled,' and adds shading, bold extrema, and expanded captions to the retraining tables. Tables are relocated or renumbered; all five figure graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Separating methodology from results, clarifying the contribution relative to CRR, and correcting Table 2’s model labels modestly improve interpretability. These gains are limited by inaccurate new aggregate statements in Section 4.5. Those errors remain localized to the summary, while the detailed appendix results and underlying empirical evidence are preserved.
